pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all existing rows are 0 and the CHECK rejects 2; migration 0002 sets NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.
test 'AC-2' asserts exact list with ★ only on the starred item.
test 'AC-3' stars 3 and 1 and asserts the exact id-ordered starred list and a 200.
test 'AC-4' checks / and ?show=all give the full id-ordered list.

The late commit f8804e0 renamed the test so it no longer names AC-5. It also rewrote the AC in the spec to 'verified by review: checked by hand', which is not a followable step. No test names AC-5, and the spec marking is vacuous. The link behaviour is implemented, but the item is unmet by the rules.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty and __proto__; the code uses Object.hasOwn.

findings.what: Commit f8804e0 ('Follow-up edits') edited AC-5 after the go. It appended '— verified by review: checked by hand' mid-sentence, which mangles the item. It records no owner decision or date. 'Checked by hand' is not a followable step. The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', which is false.
findings.fix: Revert the spec edit. Restore the AC-5 wording. Do not weaken the item without a dated owner decision.

findings.what: The same commit removed 'AC-5:' from the test title, so no test names AC-5. The test itself still checks the links and would fail if they broke.
findings.fix: Restore the title 'AC-5: each view links to the other'.

findings.what: The PR body says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but the final commit changed the spec's AC-5 and renamed a test.
findings.fix: Revert the late edits, or declare them with the owner's decision.

findings.what: The traffic-config checker is loosened to accept any query string. The PR discloses this, and the tests cover it. No spec decision covers the change, but it is needed for AC-7.
findings.fix: Optionally note it in the spec.

lenses.note: The spec exists and carries a go. The implementation matches the decisions: starred items keep id order, and the view is a query parameter.
AC-5 was reworded after the go with no owner decision. Every row of the state table has a test.
I did not run the tests (they need the cloudflare workers pool). Reading them: assertions are exact and would fail on broken code. The AC-5 label was stripped.
The README mentions ?show=starred. It does not mention the 400 for other values, which is minor.
The query is parameter-free with a whitelisted WHERE, and the view is validated with Object.hasOwn. I found no defects.
The show value is whitelisted. Titles are escaped. No injection found.
The diff touches no UI stylesheets or components. It only changes server-rendered HTML strings in src/index.js.
No browser flow or UI files are present. The page is plain generated HTML, and there are no screenshots.
The claim 'Changed after the go: nothing' is false given commit f8804e0.
